mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (more than 1% quarter-over-quarter) indicates a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (more than 0.5% in the last month) signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (more than 1% month-over-month) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (more than 5% month-over-month) signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 5% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% month-over-month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
